sanskrit: tato 'pareṇa bhallena mādhavasya dhvajottamam ciccheda samare drauṇiḥ siṃhanādaṃ nanāda ca
english: Then with another broad-headed shaft the son of Droṇa cut down Mādhava's lofty banner in the battle, and roared aloud the lion's roar.

sanskrit: punaś cainaṃ śarair ghoraiś chādayām āsa bhārata nidāghānte mahārāja yathā megho divākaram
english: And once more, O Bhārata, he covered him over with dreadful arrows, as at the end of the hot season a cloud veils the sun, O great king.

sanskrit: sātyakiś ca mahārāja śarajālaṃ nihatya tat drauṇim abhyapatat tūrṇaṃ śarajālair anekadhā
english: But Sātyaki, O great king, struck down that net of arrows and swiftly fell upon the son of Droṇa with manifold nets of arrows in turn.

sanskrit: tāpayām āsa ca drauṇiṃ śaineyaḥ paravīrahā vimukto meghajālena yathaiva tapanas tathā
english: And Śaineya, slayer of enemy heroes, scorched the son of Droṇa as the sun scorches when freed from a covering mass of clouds.

sanskrit: śarāṇāṃ ca sahasreṇa punar enaṃ samudyatam sātyakiś chādayām āsa nanāda ca mahābalaḥ
english: And as he rose up again, the mighty Sātyaki covered him over with a thousand arrows, and let forth a roar.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā putraṃ tathā grastaṃ rāhuṇeva niśākaram abhyadravata śaineyaṃ bhāradvājaḥ pratāpavān
english: Seeing his son thus seized, as the moon is seized by Rāhu, the valiant son of Bharadvāja rushed against Śaineya.

sanskrit: vivyādha ca pṛṣatkena sutīkṣṇena mahāmṛdhe parīpsan svasutaṃ rājan vārṣṇeyenābhitāpitam
english: And in that great fray he pierced him with a keenly sharpened shaft, longing, O king, to rescue his own son who was being scorched by the Vārṣṇeya.

sanskrit: sātyakis tu raṇe jitvā guruputraṃ mahāratham droṇaṃ vivyādha viṃśatyā sarvapāraśavaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: But Sātyaki, having vanquished in battle the preceptor's son, that great car-warrior, pierced Droṇa with twenty arrows all made wholly of iron.

sanskrit: tadantaram ameyātmā kaunteyaḥ śvetavāhanaḥ abhyadravad raṇe kruddho droṇaṃ prati mahārathaḥ
english: In that interval the son of Kuntī of immeasurable spirit, he of the white steeds, that great car-warrior, rushed in fury against Droṇa in the battle.

sanskrit: tato droṇaś ca pārthaś ca sameyātāṃ mahāmṛdhe yathā budhaś ca śukraś ca mahārāja nabhastale
english: Then Droṇa and Pārtha closed together in the great fray, even as Budha and Śukra meet, O great king, in the vault of heaven.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca kathaṃ droṇo maheṣvāsaḥ pāṇḍavaś ca dhanaṃjayaḥ samīyatū raṇe śūrau tan mamācakṣva saṃjaya
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: How did Droṇa the mighty archer and the Pāṇḍava Dhanaṃjaya, those two heroes, encounter each other in battle? Tell me that, Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: priyo hi pāṇḍavo nityaṃ bhāradvājasya dhīmataḥ ācāryaś ca raṇe nityaṃ priyaḥ pārthasya saṃjaya
english: For the Pāṇḍava is ever dear to the wise son of Bharadvāja, and the preceptor too is ever dear to Pārtha in battle, Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: tāv ubhau rathinau saṃkhye dṛptau siṃhāv ivotkaṭau kathaṃ samīyatur yuddhe bhāradvājadhanaṃjayau
english: Those two car-warriors, fierce in the field like two haughty lions—how did the son of Bharadvāja and Dhanaṃjaya come together in the fight?

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca na droṇaḥ samare pārthaṃ jānīte priyam ātmanaḥ kṣatradharmaṃ puraskṛtya pārtho vā gurum āhave
english: Saṃjaya said: In battle Droṇa did not regard Pārtha as one dear to himself, nor did Pārtha so regard his teacher in the fray, each setting the warrior's duty foremost.

sanskrit: na kṣatriyā raṇe rājan varjayanti parasparam nirmaryādaṃ hi yudhyante pitṛbhir bhrātṛbhiḥ saha
english: Warriors, O king, do not spare one another in battle; they fight without restraint even against fathers and brothers.

sanskrit: raṇe bhārata pārthena droṇo viddhas tribhiḥ śaraiḥ nācintayata tān bāṇān pārthacāpacyutān yudhi
english: In the battle, O Bhārata, Droṇa was pierced by Pārtha with three arrows, yet he gave no thought to those shafts loosed from Pārtha's bow in the fight.

sanskrit: śaravṛṣṭyā punaḥ pārthaś chādayām āsa taṃ raṇe prajajvāla ca roṣeṇa gahane 'gnir ivotthitaḥ
english: Again Pārtha covered him over with a rain of arrows in the battle, and Droṇa blazed up with wrath like a fire risen in a thicket.

sanskrit: tato 'rjunaṃ raṇe droṇaḥ śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ vārayām āsa rājendra nacirād iva bhārata
english: Thereupon, O lord of kings, Droṇa checked Arjuna in the battle with smooth-jointed arrows, and that almost at once, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tato duryodhano rājā suśarmāṇam acodayat droṇasya samare rājan pārṣṇigrahaṇakāraṇāt
english: Then King Duryodhana urged on Suśarman, O king, that he might guard Droṇa's rear in the battle.

sanskrit: trigartarāḍ api kruddho bhṛśam āyamya kārmukam chādayām āsa samare pārthaṃ bāṇair ayomukhaiḥ
english: And the king of the Trigartas in wrath, drawing his bow hard, covered Pārtha over in the battle with iron-faced arrows.

sanskrit: tābhyāṃ muktāḥ śarā rājann antarikṣe virejire haṃsā iva mahārāja śaratkāle nabhastale
english: The arrows loosed by those two, O king, shone in the mid-air like wild geese, O great king, in the autumn sky.

sanskrit: te śarāḥ prāpya kaunteyaṃ samastā viviśuḥ prabho phalabhāranataṃ yadvat svāduvṛkṣaṃ vihaṃgamāḥ
english: Reaching the son of Kuntī, those arrows all entered him, O lord, as birds settle upon a sweet-fruited tree bowed down with the weight of its fruit.

sanskrit: arjunas tu raṇe nādaṃ vinadya rathināṃ varaḥ trigartarājaṃ samare saputraṃ vivyadhe śaraiḥ
english: But Arjuna, foremost of car-warriors, raising a war-cry in the battle, pierced the king of the Trigartas together with his sons with his arrows.

sanskrit: te vadhyamānāḥ pārthena kāleneva yugakṣaye pārtham evābhyavartanta maraṇe kṛtaniścayāḥ mumucuḥ śaravṛṣṭiṃ ca pāṇḍavasya rathaṃ prati
english: Smitten by Pārtha as if by Time at the dissolution of an age, and resolved upon death, they turned upon Pārtha himself and loosed a rain of arrows against the Pāṇḍava's chariot.

sanskrit: śaravṛṣṭiṃ tatas tāṃ tu śaravarṣeṇa pāṇḍavaḥ pratijagrāha rājendra toyavṛṣṭim ivācalaḥ
english: That rain of arrows the Pāṇḍava then received with a downpour of his own arrows, O lord of kings, as a mountain receives a downpour of water.

sanskrit: tatrādbhutam apaśyāma bībhatsor hastalāghavam vimuktāṃ bahubhiḥ śūraiḥ śastravṛṣṭiṃ durāsadām
english: There we beheld a marvel, the lightness of Bībhatsu's hand, as he met that irresistible rain of weapons loosed by many heroes.

sanskrit: yad eko vārayām āsa māruto 'bhragaṇān iva karmaṇā tena pārthasya tutuṣur devadānavāḥ
english: For alone he warded it off, as the wind scatters the masses of clouds; at that feat of Pārtha the gods and dānavas rejoiced.

sanskrit: atha kruddho raṇe pārthas trigartān prati bhārata mumocāstraṃ mahārāja vāyavyaṃ pṛtanāmukhe
english: Then in wrath, O Bhārata, Pārtha loosed against the Trigartas in the battle the weapon of Vāyu, O great king, at the head of the host.

sanskrit: prādurāsīt tato vāyuḥ kṣobhayāṇo nabhastalam pātayan vai tarugaṇān vinighnaṃś caiva sainikān
english: Thereupon a wind arose, churning the vault of heaven, felling clusters of trees and smiting down the soldiers.

sanskrit: tato droṇo 'bhivīkṣyaiva vāyavyāstraṃ sudāruṇam śailam anyan mahārāja ghoram astraṃ mumoca ha
english: Then Droṇa, on beholding that most dreadful weapon of Vāyu, loosed in answer another terrible weapon, the weapon of the mountain, O great king.

sanskrit: droṇena yudhi nirmukte tasminn astre mahāmṛdhe praśaśāma tato vāyuḥ prasannāś cābhavan diśaḥ
english: When that weapon had been loosed by Droṇa in the great fray, the wind was stilled, and the quarters of the sky grew clear.

sanskrit: tataḥ pāṇḍusuto vīras trigartasya rathavrajān nirutsāhān raṇe cakre vimukhān viparākramān
english: Then the heroic son of Pāṇḍu made the ranks of the Trigarta cars dispirited in the battle, turned away in flight and stripped of their valor.

sanskrit: tato duryodhano rājā kṛpaś ca rathināṃ varaḥ aśvatthāmā tataḥ śalyaḥ kāmbojaś ca sudakṣiṇaḥ
english: Then King Duryodhana, and Kṛpa the foremost of car-warriors, and Aśvatthāman, and Śalya, and Sudakṣiṇa the Kāmboja,

sanskrit: vindānuvindāv āvantyau bāhlikaś ca sabāhlikaḥ mahatā rathavaṃśena pārthasyāvārayan diśaḥ
english: and Vinda and Anuvinda of Avanti, and Bāhlika with his Bāhlika host, blocked off the quarters around Pārtha with a great array of chariots.

sanskrit: tathaiva bhagadattaś ca śrutāyuś ca mahābalaḥ gajānīkena bhīmasya tāv avārayatāṃ diśaḥ
english: In the same way Bhagadatta and the mighty Śrutāyus, those two, with their host of elephants blocked off the quarters around Bhīma.

sanskrit: bhūriśravāḥ śalaś caiva saubalaś ca viśāṃ pate śaraughair vividhais tūrṇaṃ mādrīputrāv avārayan
english: Bhūriśravas and Śala, and the son of Subala, O lord of peoples, swiftly hemmed in the two sons of Mādrī with manifold floods of arrows.

sanskrit: bhīṣmas tu sahitaḥ sarvair dhārtarāṣṭrasya sainikaiḥ yudhiṣṭhiraṃ samāsādya sarvataḥ paryavārayat
english: But Bhīṣma, joined by all the soldiers of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son, closed in upon Yudhiṣṭhira and surrounded him on every side.

sanskrit: āpatantaṃ gajānīkaṃ dṛṣṭvā pārtho vṛkodaraḥ lelihan sṛkkiṇī vīro mṛgarāḍ iva kānane
english: Seeing the host of elephants bearing down upon him, the heroic Vṛkodara, son of Pṛthā, licked the corners of his mouth like the king of beasts in the forest.

sanskrit: tatas tu rathināṃ śreṣṭho gadāṃ gṛhya mahāhave avaplutya rathāt tūrṇaṃ tava sainyam abhīṣayat
english: Then that foremost of car-warriors, taking up his mace in the great battle, leaped down swiftly from his chariot and struck terror into your army.

sanskrit: tam udvīkṣya gadāhastaṃ tatas te gajasādinaḥ parivavrū raṇe yattā bhīmasenaṃ samantataḥ
english: Beholding him mace in hand, those elephant-riders, intent on the fight, surrounded Bhīmasena on every side in the battle.

sanskrit: gajamadhyam anuprāptaḥ pāṇḍavaś ca vyarājata meghajālasya mahato yathā madhyagato raviḥ
english: And the Pāṇḍava, come into the midst of the elephants, shone forth like the sun set in the midst of a great mass of clouds.

sanskrit: vyadhamat sa gajānīkaṃ gadayā pāṇḍavarṣabhaḥ mahābhrajālam atulaṃ mātariśveva saṃtatam
english: That bull among the Pāṇḍavas scattered the host of elephants with his mace, as the wind scatters a vast unbroken expanse of mighty clouds.

sanskrit: te vadhyamānā balinā bhīmasenena dantinaḥ ārtanādaṃ raṇe cakrur garjanto jaladā iva
english: Those tusked beasts, slaughtered by the mighty Bhīmasena, raised cries of anguish in the battle, roaring like rain-clouds.

sanskrit: bahudhā dāritaś caiva viṣāṇais tatra dantibhiḥ phullāśokanibhaḥ pārthaḥ śuśubhe raṇamūrdhani
english: Gashed in many places there by the tusks of the elephants, the son of Pṛthā, resembling a blossoming aśoka tree, shone splendid at the head of the battle.

sanskrit: viṣāṇe dantinaṃ gṛhya nirviṣāṇam athākarot viṣāṇena ca tenaiva kumbhe 'bhyāhatya dantinam pātayām āsa samare daṇḍahasta ivāntakaḥ
english: Seizing a tusker by the tusk, he wrenched that tusk away, and with that very tusk smiting the elephant upon its frontal globe, he struck it down in the battle like Death wielding his rod.

sanskrit: śoṇitāktāṃ gadāṃ bibhran medomajjākṛtacchaviḥ kṛtāṅgadaḥ śoṇitena rudravat pratyadṛśyata
english: Bearing his blood-smeared mace, his hue made of fat and marrow, with armlets fashioned of gore, he appeared like Rudra to behold.

sanskrit: evaṃ te vadhyamānās tu hataśeṣā mahāgajāḥ prādravanta diśo rājan vimṛdnantaḥ svakaṃ balam
english: Thus slaughtered, the great elephants that survived the slaughter fled in all directions, O king, trampling their own forces underfoot.

sanskrit: dravadbhis tair mahānāgaiḥ samantād bharatarṣabha duryodhanabalaṃ sarvaṃ punar āsīt parāṅmukham
english: By those great elephants fleeing on every side, O bull of the Bhāratas, the whole army of Duryodhana was once again turned to flight.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca madhyāhne tu mahārāja saṃgrāmaḥ samapadyata lokakṣayakaro raudro bhīṣmasya saha somakaiḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: At midday, O great king, there arose a fierce battle, destroyer of the world, between Bhīṣma and the Somakas.

sanskrit: gāṅgeyo rathināṃ śreṣṭhaḥ pāṇḍavānām anīkinīm vyadhaman niśitair bāṇaiḥ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: The son of Gaṅgā, foremost of car-warriors, scattered the host of the Pāṇḍavas with his whetted arrows by the hundreds and by the thousands.

sanskrit: saṃmamarda ca tat sainyaṃ pitā devavratas tava dhānyānām iva lūnānāṃ prakaraṃ gogaṇā iva
english: And your father Devavrata crushed that army as herds of cattle crush a heap of reaped grain.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnaḥ śikhaṇḍī ca virāṭo drupadas tathā bhīṣmam āsādya samare śarair jaghnur mahāratham
english: Dhṛṣṭadyumna and Śikhaṇḍin, and Virāṭa and Drupada, closing with Bhīṣma in the battle, smote that great car-warrior with their arrows.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ tato viddhvā virāṭaṃ ca tribhiḥ śaraiḥ drupadasya ca nārācaṃ preṣayām āsa bhārata
english: Then, having pierced Dhṛṣṭadyumna and Virāṭa with three arrows, he sped an iron shaft at Drupada, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tena viddhā maheṣvāsā bhīṣmeṇāmitrakarśinā cukrudhuḥ samare rājan pādaspṛṣṭā ivoragāḥ
english: Pierced by Bhīṣma, the tormentor of foes, those mighty archers blazed with wrath in the battle, O king, like serpents trodden underfoot.

sanskrit: śikhaṇḍī taṃ ca vivyādha bharatānāṃ pitāmaham strīmayaṃ manasā dhyātvā nāsmai prāharad acyutaḥ
english: Śikhaṇḍin pierced that grandsire of the Bhāratas; but the steadfast one, reflecting in his mind that this was one born of woman, struck no blow against him.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnas tu samare krodhād agnir iva jvalan pitāmahaṃ tribhir bāṇair bāhvor urasi cārpayat
english: But Dhṛṣṭadyumna, blazing like fire with wrath in the battle, planted three arrows in the grandsire's arms and breast.

sanskrit: drupadaḥ pañcaviṃśatyā virāṭo daśabhiḥ śaraiḥ śikhaṇḍī pañcaviṃśatyā bhīṣmaṃ vivyādha sāyakaiḥ
english: Drupada with twenty-five, Virāṭa with ten arrows, and Śikhaṇḍin with twenty-five shafts pierced Bhīṣma.

sanskrit: so 'tividdho mahārāja bhīṣmaḥ saṃkhye mahātmabhiḥ vasante puṣpaśabalo raktāśoka ivābabhau
english: Sorely pierced, O great king, by those high-souled warriors in the field, Bhīṣma shone like a red aśoka in spring, dappled with blossoms.

sanskrit: tān pratyavidhyad gāṅgeyas tribhis tribhir ajihmagaiḥ drupadasya ca bhallena dhanuś ciccheda māriṣa
english: The son of Gaṅgā pierced them in return, each with three straight-flying shafts, and with a broad-headed arrow he cut Drupada's bow, O honored one.

sanskrit: so 'nyat kārmukam ādāya bhīṣmaṃ vivyādha pañcabhiḥ sārathiṃ ca tribhir bāṇaiḥ suśitai raṇamūrdhani
english: Taking up another bow, he pierced Bhīṣma with five arrows and his charioteer with three well-whetted shafts at the head of the battle.

sanskrit: tato bhīmo mahārāja draupadyāḥ pañca cātmajāḥ kekayā bhrātaraḥ pañca sātyakiś caiva sātvataḥ
english: Then Bhīma, O great king, and the five sons of Draupadī, and the five Kekaya brothers, and Sātyaki of the Sātvata line,

sanskrit: abhyadravanta gāṅgeyaṃ yudhiṣṭhirahitepsayā rirakṣiṣantaḥ pāñcālyaṃ dhṛṣṭadyumnamukhan raṇe
english: rushed against the son of Gaṅgā, seeking Yudhiṣṭhira's welfare and wishing to protect the Pāñcāla Dhṛṣṭadyumna who led them in the battle.

sanskrit: tathaiva tāvakāḥ sarve bhīṣmarakṣārtham udyatāḥ pratyudyayuḥ pāṇḍusenāṃ sahasainyā narādhipa
english: And in like manner all your warriors, set upon guarding Bhīṣma, advanced with their hosts against the Pāṇḍava army, O ruler of men.

sanskrit: tatrāsīt sumahad yuddhaṃ tava teṣāṃ ca saṃkulam narāśvarathanāgānāṃ yamarāṣṭravivardhanam
english: There was a vast and confused battle between your men and theirs, of men and horses and chariots and elephants, swelling the realm of Yama.

sanskrit: rathī rathinam āsādya prāhiṇod yamasādanam tathetarān samāsādya naranāgāśvasādinaḥ
english: A car-warrior, closing with a car-warrior, sent him to the abode of Yama; so too with others, the riders of men and elephants and horses, closing in,

sanskrit: anayan paralokāya śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ astraiś ca vividhair ghorais tatra tatra viśāṃ pate
english: led them to the other world with smooth-jointed arrows and with manifold dreadful weapons, here and there, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: rathāś ca rathibhir hīnā hatasārathayas tathā vipradrutāśvāḥ samare diśo jagmuḥ samantataḥ
english: Chariots bereft of their warriors and with their charioteers slain, their horses bolting away, ran in all directions over the battlefield.

sanskrit: mardamānā narān rājan hayāṃś ca subahūn raṇe vātāyamānā dṛśyante gandharvanagaropamāḥ
english: Crushing men and very many horses in the battle, O king, and rushing like the wind, they were seen resembling the cities of the gandharvas.

sanskrit: rathinaś ca rathair hīnā varmiṇas tejasā yutāḥ kuṇḍaloṣṇīṣiṇaḥ sarve niṣkāṅgadavibhūṣitāḥ
english: Car-warriors bereft of their chariots, clad in armor and endowed with splendor, all wearing earrings and turbans and adorned with golden chains and armlets,

sanskrit: devaputrasamā rūpe śaurye śakrasamā yudhi ṛddhyā vaiśravaṇaṃ cāti nayena ca bṛhaspatim
english: in form like the sons of the gods, in valor in battle like Śakra, surpassing Vaiśravaṇa in wealth and Bṛhaspati in statecraft,

sanskrit: sarvalokeśvarāḥ śūrās tatra tatra viśāṃ pate vipradrutā vyadṛśyanta prākṛtā iva mānavāḥ
english: those lords of all the world, those heroes, were seen fleeing here and there, O lord of peoples, like common men.

sanskrit: dantinaś ca naraśreṣṭha vihīnā varasādibhiḥ mṛdnantaḥ svāny anīkāni saṃpetuḥ sarvaśabdagāḥ
english: And the elephants, O best of men, deprived of their excellent riders, trampling their own ranks, rushed about, hurrying toward every sound.

sanskrit: varmabhiś cāmaraiś chatraiḥ patākābhiś ca māriṣa kakṣyābhir atha tottraiś ca ghaṇṭābhis tomarais tathā
english: With their armor and yak-tail fans and parasols and banners, O honored one, with their girths and goads and bells and lances likewise,

sanskrit: viśīrṇair vipradhāvanto dṛśyante sma diśo daśa nagameghapratīkāśair jaladodayanisvanaiḥ
english: all torn and shattered, they were seen running through the ten directions, those elephants like mountains or clouds, their cries like the rumble of a rising rain-cloud.

sanskrit: tathaiva dantibhir hīnān gajārohān viśāṃ pate pradhāvanto 'nvapaśyāma tava teṣāṃ ca saṃkule
english: In the same way we beheld elephant-riders bereft of their tuskers running about, O lord of peoples, in the confusion of your men and theirs.

sanskrit: nānādeśasamutthāṃś ca turagān hemabhūṣitān vātāyamānān adrākṣaṃ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: And horses arisen from many lands, decked with gold, rushing like the wind, I saw by the hundreds and by the thousands.

sanskrit: aśvārohān hatair aśvair gṛhītāsīn samantataḥ dravamāṇān apaśyāma drāvyamāṇāṃś ca saṃyuge
english: Horsemen whose mounts were slain, grasping their swords, we saw on every side fleeing and being driven in flight in the battle.

sanskrit: gajo gajaṃ samāsādya dravamāṇaṃ mahāraṇe yayau vimṛdnaṃs tarasā padātīn vājinas tathā
english: An elephant, charging upon a fleeing elephant in the great battle, rushed on, crushing in its course the foot-soldiers and the horses.

sanskrit: tathaiva ca rathān rājan saṃmamarda raṇe gajaḥ rathaś caiva samāsādya padātiṃ turagaṃ tathā
english: And likewise an elephant, O king, crushed chariots in the battle; and a chariot too, bearing down upon foot-soldier and horse alike,

sanskrit: vyamṛdnāt samare rājaṃs turagāṃś ca narān raṇe evaṃ te bahudhā rājan pramṛdnantaḥ parasparam
english: crushed horses and men in the battle, O king. Thus did they, O king, in manifold ways trample one another.
